news.title:
MarketsMojo rates Karur Vysya Bank Ltd. as Buy, updated on 13 May 2026.
The analysis reflects the stock's fundamentals and performance as of 25 May 2026.

Karur Vysya Bank shows a structured uptrend but is in consolidation; key levels: support at ₹275, resistance at ₹300.
DCB Bank is range-bound between ₹160-₹200; City Union Bank trades within ₹242-₹255 with low momentum.
KARURVYSYA: Future Stability Will Depend On Leadership Reappointments And Dividend Decisions
news.body: Analysts have maintained Karur Vysya Bank's fair value estimate at around ₹305. The updated price target reflects revised assumptions for the discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E, rather than a significant shift in their overall view.

news.title: KARURVYSYA: Steadier Outlook Will Hinge On Leadership Continuity And Governance Decisions
news.body: Analysts have lifted their price target for Karur Vysya Bank from about ₹222 to roughly ₹305, citing updated assumptions for revenue growth, profit margin, and future P/E that they believe support a higher fair value estimate. What's in the News A board meeting is scheduled for May 7, 2026 to consider and approve the audited financial results for the quarter and year ended March 31, 2026, and to recommend any dividend on the equity shares.

news.title: Price target increased by 9.6% to ₹353
news.body: Up from ₹322, the current price target is an average from 15 analysts. New target price is 19% above last closing price of ₹297. Stock is up 69% over the past year. The company is forecast to post earnings per share of ₹28.16 for next year compared to ₹25.98 last year.

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹25.98 (vs ₹20.11 in FY 2025)
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹25.98 (up from ₹20.11 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹62.7b (up 15% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹25.1b (up 29% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 40% (up from 36% in FY 2025). The increase in margin was driven by higher revenue. Revenue is forecast to grow 6.3% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 1.4% growth forecast for the Banks industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 24% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 56% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.
